One entry per line: a domain with its subdomains (example.com) or a list from the geodata set (geosite:youtube). TCP to these sites goes directly, past the server, and the start of TLS goes in small pieces; QUIC (UDP 443) to them is closed, so apps switch to TCP. May help against filters that look for the site name; does not help if the address itself is blocked. Works while connected to a server and, when there are no servers, without one; applies right away.

When there are no servers but “Sites directly with splitting” has entries (or other sites are split too), “Connect” starts a tunnel without a server. With servers, the connection goes only through them. Without a server it helps only against filters that look for the site name: a blocked address stays blocked.

Sends the start of the secure connection to the server (TLS ClientHello) in small pieces. May help against filters that look for the site name there; not everywhere, and it adds tens of milliseconds to connecting. Only servers with TLS or REALITY over TCP; applies right away.

Components inside DPpass and their licenses

DPpass has no telemetry, analytics or crash reports and doesn’t read device identifiers. Subscriptions get only their link, DPpass’s own User-Agent and — if you turn it on — a random device ID. Network check — when you tap it and, unless turned off in settings, after the network changes while the VPN is on — contacts ya.ru, speed.cloudflare.com and www.google.com and sends nothing about you. The log and report stay on the phone.
What the network lets through right now

DPpass checks, one at a time, what this network lets through: names, connections, secure connections, QUIC and a large transfer — to ya.ru, speed.cloudflare.com and www.google.com, past the tunnel. Nothing about you or the phone is sent; these sites see the phone’s address, as when opening a page.
For your information only: the result doesn’t change how a server is chosen yet. Repeated checks are paced — skipped steps are not network failures.
Checks are paced: frequent probes can themselves trigger blocking. Try again in %1$d s.
The network is already being checked after it changed. The result will be used for connecting; try again in a minute.
skipped: too soon after the previous check

Ping, jitter and download speed through the server DPpass is connected to: 10 small requests and a download of up to 25 MB (no longer than 8 s) from speed.cloudflare.com through the server. On a mobile network this counts against your plan. The next measurement is available a minute later.
Connect DPpass: speed is measured through the server.
Data stopped %1$s s into the download (%2$s Mbit/s until then) and nothing came after: this looks like the connection being frozen, not a slow link.

The connection plan has no randomness: the server you chose goes first, then the last good one, then by health, latency and transport class. Here is what the plan decided and why.
